verdicts.claim: User-Agent required; rate limits 'reasonable' and undisclosed; retry typically within 5 seconds; formats GeoJSON/JSON-LD/DWML/CAP/OXML/ATOM; /points and /gridpoints endpoints; re-check /points periodically
verdicts.note: Page fetched 2026-08-22. Verbatim: 'A User Agent is required to identify your application'; 'The rate limit is not public information, but allows a generous amount for typical use'; 'may be retried after the limit clears (typically within 5 seconds)'; formats listed are GeoJSON, JSON-LD, DWML, OXML, CAP, ATOM; /points/{lat},{lon} -> grid endpoint; 'it is necessary to check back to the /points endpoint periodically'. Wording nit: the page says 'generous', not 'reasonable'. Nothing on the page says a contact e-mail in User-Agent raises the limit.

verdicts.claim: NWS may block IPs impacting service; align requests to data refresh cycles; contact sdm@noaa.gov
verdicts.note: Page says NWS 'may find it necessary to block IP addresses or query types'; 'If the forecast data is updated every 6 hours you should only make requests during those cycle output windows'; 'Users who find that their queries are blocked should send an email to sdm@noaa.gov'. Also gives guidance to retry at 1-minute intervals when services are unavailable and to poll 'once or twice a minute' at most for short-fused warnings. No numeric limit is stated.

ASNOW: 1-h and 6-h deterministic, exceedance probabilities (>0.00254 ... >0.3048 m), and 15 percentile levels (1,5,10,20,25,30,40,50,60,70,75,80,90,95,99%). FICEAC present. corrections: Gridpoint example URL mismatch: https://api.weather.gov/gridpoints/SEW/124,67 is not the Sedro-Woolley cell (its elevation is 0.9 m). /points/48.50,-122.24 resolves to forecastGridData https://api.weather.gov/gridpoints/SEW/136,109 — use 136,109 in all examples and code.

Rate-limit wording: the NWS API docs say the limit 'is not public information, but allows a generous amount for typical use', not 'reasonable'. Neither the docs page nor the api.weather.gov FAQ (weather-gov.github.io/api/general-faqs) documents any mechanism by which a registered User-Agent/contact raises the limit; state this as undocumented. The abusive-user page adds practical ceilings: retry no faster than 1-minute intervals when unavailable and poll at most 'once or twice a minute' even for short-fused warnings.

Product retention: api.weather.gov does not document a retention period. Observed on 2026-08-22: oldest KSEW AFD 2026-08-15T10:10Z, oldest KSEW ZFP 2026-08-15T09:37Z, oldest national FLW 2026-08-15T10:51Z (all ~7 days). The weather.gov/wrh/TextProduct page states its text-product database 'contains products that were issued in the past 168 hours (7 days)'; cite it as corroborating context, not as an API guarantee, and keep the 7-day figure labelled as observed.

NBM v5.0 implementation date: vlab.noaa.gov/web/mdl/nbm says 'The NBM has upgraded to version 5.0 as of May 5, 2026'. SCN 26-24 Updated (AAC, 28 Apr 2026) itself says 'On or about Thursday, April 30, 2026, beginning with the 1300 UTC model run', with a Critical-Weather-Day fallback of 1300 UTC Monday May 4, 2026. Attribute 'May 5, 2026' to the vlab page, not to SCN 26-24.

NBM CONUS 2.5 km can be de-INFERENCED: 'Cycles, Projections, and Domains in the NBM v5.0' (https://vlab.noaa.gov/documents/6609493/50324479/NBM_Cycles_and_Domains_v5_0.pdf, Table 1) gives CONUS 2.5 km (2345 x 1597), Alaska 3 km, Hawaii 2.5 km, Puerto Rico 1.25 km, Guam 2.5 km, Oceanic 10 km, Global 50 km. The same document states the Core Blend output cadence: hourly to 48 h, 3-hourly to 192 h, 6-hourly to 264 h (with 3-h/6-h projections shifted so valid times stay divisible by 3/6 for cycles not divisible by 6).

Why QMD goes to f276 while core stops at f264: per the same Cycles/Domains document, QMD '1-hour accumulated precipitation (CONUS only): Projections are available hourly out to 276 hours'; 6- and 12-h QPF 6-hourly to 276 h; 24/48/72-h QPF 12-hourly to 276 h; other QMD elements hourly to 60 h, 3-hourly to 204 h, 6-hourly to 276 h. QMD runs only for the 00/06/12/18Z cycles and 'starts 6 hours and 40 minutes after the named cycle ... and finishes within an hour' (the Blend_Precip_QMD_v5.0 doc says 'delayed by approximately 6.5 hours'). Observed: 12Z qmd f001 LastModified 19:16:29Z, f276 19:26:59Z — i.e. ~7.3 h latency, versus ~72-78 min for core. The research summary's latency statement must distinguish core from qmd.

NBM v5.0 timing table: NBM_v5.0_Timing_Differences.pdf (https://vlab.noaa.gov/documents/6609493/49238069/NBM_v5.0_Timing_Differences.pdf) lists only deltas relative to v4.3, not absolute times: NOMADS Core, all cycles, AK/CO/GU/HI/PR/OC: 20-30 min delay; NOMADS QMD CO: 06/18Z 5-10 min early, 00Z 10 min delay, 12Z 5-10 min delay; NOMADS text bulletins 00/12Z 20-40 min delay, 01/13Z 5-10 min early, 07/19Z 5-15 min delay. Absolute schedule comes from the Cycles/Domains doc: Core Blend starts 10 min before the hour (00Z cycle begins 23:50Z) and aims to finish within one hour; key cycles are 01/07/13/19Z. The observed 72-78 min remains the best CONUS-core number.

SNOWLVL definition is now sourced: Blend_Winter_v5_0_Configuration_and_Technical_Details.pdf states 'Definition of Snow Level: The altitude where the wet-bulb temperature first crosses above 0.5°' C, computed from vertical wet-bulb profiles, with a 9-point smoother applied, and 15 weighted percentiles (0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99). Rewrite 'percentiles 1-99' as 'fifteen percentiles from 1st to 99th'. The idx string '0 m above mean sea level' is the GRIB2 fixed-surface (MSL) descriptor, not the unit of the value.

Core f024 idx also carries an APCP 12-24 hour 'prob >0.254' record in addition to the 1-h and 6-h ones; list it. SCN 26-24 also states that NOMADS hosts both core and qmd master files at https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/blend/prod/ with names core/blend.tCCz.core.fHHH.rg.grib2 and qmd/blend.tCCz.qmd.fHHH.rg.grib2, and that the global domain is core-only.

S3 listing pagination: the cited prefix listing (core ... .f0) is truncated at 1000 keys and only reaches f159 on its own (IsTruncated=true). Document that a full per-cycle inventory needs a continuation marker or multiple prefixes (f0/f1/f2).

HRRR/RRFS: SCN 26-48 Updated (aab, https://www.weather.gov/media/notification/pdf_2026/scn26-048_RRFS_and_REFS_Implementation.aab.pdf) confirms RRFS/REFS production implementation October 6, 2026 (12 UTC) with parallel NOMADS output from August 11, 2026; an earlier 'aaa' revision dated June 2, 2026 still said Aug 31, 2026 — cite the aab revision. SCN 26-47 (aaa) retires NAM, SREF, HREF, HiresW (except Guam) and NAM MOS on October 6, 2026; HRRR and RAP are not on the retirement list, and SCN 26-48 says 'For the Alaska and CONUS REFS domains, the HRRR provides two additional members (from current and 6 h old cycles)'. No HRRR retirement date exists in any SCN found; keep that as an open item.

Alerts: the 'parameters' sub-keys (NWSheadline, VTEC, AWIPSidentifier, WMOidentifier, BLOCKCHANNEL, eventEndingTime) vary by alert; code must treat them as optional. Per-location product-type lists (/products/locations/SEW/types) are a rolling ~7-day window and change daily (HWO was absent for KSEW on 2026-08-22), so do not hard-code them.
